item.title: Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, resigns after allegations of improper conduct
item.description:
U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio unveil a plaque at the Greek foreign ministry in Athens on Oct. 7, 2026. Mark Schiefelbein/AFP via Getty Images The United States is down one more ambassador. On Oct. 13, 2026, it emerged that President Donald Trump had asked Kimberly Guilfoyle, a MAGA loyalist and ex-fiancée of Trump’s son Donald Jr., to resign her position as U.S. ambassador to Greece , a NATO ally. It follows allegations that the Trump adviser turned diplomat pushed for a Republican donor to pay off her six-figure American Express bill . Guilfoyle later confirmed that she would comply with the request and resigned . In so doing, Athens became one of a number of U.S. overseas missions with a vacancy at the top. In fact, 93 out of 196 U.S. ambassador jobs are currently unfilled. And that is after U.S. senators confirmed 10 new…

item.title: Pope walking and recovering 'as expected' after surgery, doctors say
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV had his lung nodule surgically removed. AP Photo/Aurelien Morissard When many people think of an average lung cancer patient, they often imagine an older man smoking . But the face of lung cancer has changed. Over the past 15 years, more women, never smokers and younger people are being diagnosed with lung cancer. In fact, lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death among women , and more women die from lung cancer than breast, ovarian and colorectal cancer each year. The American Lung Association reports that while lung cancer rates have risen by 79% for women over the last 44 years, they decreased by 43% for men . And for the first time in history, there are more young women than men diagnosed with lung cancer. News about Pope Leo XIV’s lung cancer diagnosis on Oct. 13, 2026, sparked discussion about increasing rates of the disease among people who have never smoked.…

item.title: Starlink restriction 'no surprise' after Musk condemned Ukraine strikes on Russian data centres
item.description:
Restrictions reported by Ukraine on its use of the US satellite internet system Starlink have exposed Kyiv's reliance on the technology for both offensive and defensive operations in its fight against Russia'a invasion, analysts and observers say. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, David Galbreath Professor of War and Technology at the University of Bath, says that "we always knew that allowing a private organisation like Starlink to have such a big impact on the combat operations in Ukraine was going to be challenging", explaining that "it is no surprise" that Starlink services had been throttled after SpaceX boss Elon Musk called the targeting by Ukrainian drones of data services in Russia "a step too far".

Covered by 1 corporate, 2 public.
Sources: BBC News, CBS News, France 24

item.title: How Starlink disruptions affected Ukraine's battlefield operations
item.description:
Ukraine is heavily reliant on Starlink for military operations. Inna Varenytsia/REUTERS Ukrainian officials said on Wednesday that Kyiv's access to Starlink has been disrupted. Slower-than-normal speeds have affected military operations, the officials said. Ukraine is heavily reliant on Starlink, specifically for communications and drone missions. Ukraine's access to Starlink internet service was suddenly disrupted for unknown reasons, interfering with military operations, sources in the country's defense ministry and a top presidential advisor said Wednesday morning. Serhii Beskrestnov, a top advisor to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said in a social media post that Elon Musk's SpaceX had implemented speed limits for Starlink terminals overnight. item.title: Fraternity culture under scrutiny in wake of Cornell allegations
item.description:
Cornell University will ban parties and social events at fraternity houses until the end of the academic year, its president said on Tuesday, responding to the outcry over an alleged gang rape on ‌campus in 2024. The measure is the strongest reaction yet from Cornell's leadership to a lawsuit ⁠filed by a former undergraduate, Jane Doe, alleging seven men sexually assaulted her during a party. Over the last several weeks, the Ivy League school in Ithaca, New York, and its ‌president, Michael Kotlikoff, have come under heavy criticism over its response to ⁠the allegations.

item.title: Houthis launch fresh wave of missiles across Saudi Arabia
item.description:
Civilians warned to leave target area near Sana’a before attacks as conflict between Riyadh and Houthi forces escalates Saudi Arabia has launched a series of strikes on a strategic oil depot on the outskirts of Yemen’s capital, Sana’a, while later on Tuesday it said it had intercepted missiles launched toward Dharan, location of the headquarters of the huge national energy company Saudi Aramco. The attacks on both sides were a fresh escalation of the conflict between Riyadh and the Iran-backed Houthi forces. Before its offensive on Tuesday, a Saudi spokesperson warned civilians to leave the target area, in an apparent attempt to strike fear into the local population before the biggest attack so far on Houthi energy infrastructure. item.description:

item.title: Iran-backed Houthis strike Saudi oil company Aramco's headquarters, officials say
item.description:
Iran-backed Houthi fighters reportedly hit the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s national oil company in overnight strikes, stoking a conflict that risks spiralling into a wider war. The attacks follow a Houthi onslaught that killed 13, injured hundreds, and forced Riyadh’s airport to shut at least through Saturday, denting the kingdom’s reputation for stability and piling pressure on the country’s de facto ruler . Analysts fear the conflict could expand beyond the Arabian Peninsula: The Houthis are reportedly building an advanced missile using Chinese parts. US President Donald Trump has accused the group of “ purposefully trying to drive up Oil Prices ” ahead of November’s midterm elections; Tehran is reportedly targeting crude tankers in a bid to keep prices elevated. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

item.title: Inflation sizzled in September — and Social Security benefits will get a boost
item.description:
Social Security is upping monthly payments by $75 to counter inflation. About 7.3 million seniors will see increased payments starting in December, and over 72 million Social Security beneficiaries will see the $75 monthly adjustment starting in January 2027, the administration announced on Wednesday. “Social Security will implement this cost-of-living adjustment for 76 million Americans, giving them greater financial stability,” said Social Security Commissioner Frank J. Bisignano. “Under President Donald J. Trump, Social Security is delivering better, faster, higher-quality service for the American people.” The agency noted that the cost-of-living adjustment will be 3.6%, the largest adjustment in four years. item.title: Bank of America fined $1.2bn for money-laundering failures
item.description:
The Treasury Department on Tuesday announced more than $1.2 billion in penalties against Bank of America for years of failures to report suspicious transactions and address shortcomings in its anti-money-laundering program. Why it matters: The action includes the third-largest penalty in Treasury history. What they're saying: "Today's actions send a clear message that even the biggest financial institutions are not above the law," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a press release . The big picture: The civil action comes less than a week after federal regulators fined American Express $350 million over similar failures to detect and report suspected money laundering. Zoom in: Bank of America admitted to willfully violating federal anti-money-laundering laws — including requirements to maintain adequate safeguards and report suspicious transactions. item.title: North Korea says it tested cruise missiles to be launched from sub
item.description:
North Korea test-fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles on Wednesday, state media KCNA reported Thursday, saying the launches posed no threat to neighbouring countries. The tests follow heightened tensions with South Korea after a September 21 landmine explosion in the Demilitarised Zone injured three South Korean soldiers.

item.title: Student protests in Albania turn violent as demonstrators clash with police
item.description:
Dozens of people detained after government building and two banks set on fire as tens of thousands march over education costs and corruption Tens of thousands of students have taken to the streets of Tirana, the Albanian capital, setting alight a government building and two banks and hurling stones at police during a protest over rising education costs and ⁠corruption. Police responded with water ⁠cannon and teargas to disperse protesters who started a fire at the ministry of education building, overturned bins and smashed the fronts of local businesses.
